note.text:
Fixed assets (class 2) are goods kept for a long time to use in the business: land, buildings, machines, vehicles, furniture, computers, software.
Classification: intangible (21: software, patents), tangible (22 land, 23 buildings, 24 equipment, 245 vehicles), financial (27: shares, deposits).
Acquisition cost = purchase price − discounts + costs needed to make the asset ready (transport, installation, customs duties).
Entry for a purchase on credit: debit the asset account (for example 245 Transport equipment), credit 481 Suppliers of fixed assets. If paid at once: credit 521 Bank or 571 Cash.
Self-constructed assets: when the business builds its own asset (a warehouse built by its workers), the cost is recorded in the asset account and credited to account 72 (own production of fixed assets).

questions.prompt: Which kind of fixed asset is {X.s}?

misconceptions.explain: Ask: can you touch it (tangible), is it a right or software (intangible), or an investment (financial)?

solution: Intangible: no physical form (software, patents); tangible: physical (land, machines, vehicles); financial: shares, deposits.

pick.q: A machine is bought on credit. Which account is credited?
e: That is for goods to resell.
pick.y: The supplier of the asset is owed.

pick.q: A business builds its own warehouse. Which account is credited for the cost?

right.text: A vehicle is a tangible fixed asset.
Installation costs are part of the acquisition cost.

wrong.text: Goods bought to resell are fixed assets.
Transport costs are never part of the acquisition cost.
A machine bought on credit is credited to 701 Sales.
